Vocabulary specific to the two tickets in scope:

MOCK3-1 (fare boundary, mock-a): The bug is in fareFor in src/fares.ts. The condition `rider.age > 65` excludes riders aged exactly 65 from the concession fare; the JSDoc says "Riders aged 65 AND OVER pay the concession fare," so the correct operator is `>=`. totalFor delegates to fareFor, so any change to fareFor's return value propagates through totalFor automatically. The existing test suite (test/fares.test.ts) tests age 70 but not age 65 — the boundary value itself is untested. When deriving vocabulary for this guard, use the terms: fareFor, totalFor, BASE_FARE_CENTS, CONCESSION_FARE_CENTS, Rider, age, hasPass, concession fare, boundary condition, off-by-one.

MOCK3-2 (departure board, mock-b): The bug is in formatStops in src/schedule.ts. The loop condition `i < stops.length - 1` skips the final stop; the correct condition is `i < stops.length`. totalMinutes is a separate function that already reads the last element correctly and is not affected by this fix. The existing test suite (test/schedule.test.ts) only checks that the output contains '->' and the first stop name ('Union'); it does not assert the presence of the last stop ('Eglinton'). When deriving vocabulary for this guard, use the terms: formatStops, totalMinutes, Stop, stops, departure board, loop bound, off-by-one, final stop.
